stem: A client receives IV adenosine for a supraventricular tachycardia. Which transient effect should the nurse teach the client may occur immediately after administration?

options.A: Brief flushing or chest pressure that resolves rapidly.
options.B: Several hours of deep sedation after the dose.
options.C: Persistent severe pain that normally requires opioid treatment.
options.D: No noticeable sensation because adenosine produces no transient symptoms.

rationale: Adenosine has an extremely short plasma half-life and commonly causes brief, rapidly self-limiting reactions such as facial flushing and chest discomfort or pressure. Prolonged sedation and persistent severe pain are not expected label-described effects.
educational_objective: Recognize common brief adverse effects of IV adenosine.
source_locator: Clinical Pharmacology—half-life; Adverse Reactions—facial flushing and chest discomfort/pressure
source_claim_supported: Adenosine has a half-life under 10 seconds; flushing and chest discomfort are reported and adverse effects are generally rapidly self-limiting.
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported 'lasting discomfort' framing and non-label 'impending doom' wording.
audit_findings: Label directly supports brief flushing/chest discomfort.
Distractors describe effects not characteristic of adenosine.
Independent second pass found one best answer.
